Operator: Good day, and welcome to the NovaTel Communications Q2 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your touchtone phone if using a telephone, or click the Q&A button in the webcast platform if joining online. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to NovaTel Communications' Q2 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Lena Patel, Chief Network Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report our results for Q2. We exceeded expectations in several key areas. First, our customer retention metrics reached new lows, reflecting the strength of our loyalty initiatives and network enhancements. Second, our spectrum portfolio is delivering exceptional utilization rates, fueling capacity for surging data demands. We are seeing very positive results from our investments in TeleStream+, and its bundling synergies across wireless and streaming are driving meaningful ARPU uplift. Third, we executed aggressively on cost management, unlocking significant efficiencies. Fourth, our network investment discipline is positioning us for scalable growth. Finally, we are strategically positioning ourselves for accelerated subscriber additions and revenue expansion through converged services.

Michael Chen: Thank you, Alex. Turning to the financials, our revenue for the quarter was $15.2 billion, up 4.2% year-over-year. Our adjusted EBITDA was $5.85 billion, resulting in a margin of 38.5%. We are maintaining strict cost discipline. Capital expenditures were $4.5 billion, primarily allocated to 5G rollout and fiber expansion.

Let me expand on some of these highlights, starting with our churn rate performance, which is a vital indicator of our customer retention prowess and its influence on lifetime value, ARPU consistency, and sustained EBITDA margins. In Q2, our blended postpaid churn rate across mobile, broadband, and video services registered at 1.12%, reflecting a 15 basis point improvement from the prior quarter and a strong 22 basis point drop year-over-year. This marks our lowest quarterly churn in three years, surpassing the industry average of 1.45% for Tier 1 telcos according to New Street Research benchmarks.

Diving into segments, mobile postpaid churn landed at 0.78%, down 12 basis points sequentially and 18 basis points annually, achieving a multi-year low. This improvement stems from our rapid 5G Ultra Wideband expansion, now reaching 85% of our top 100 U.S. metro markets—matching Verizon's coverage but enhanced by our superior mid-band spectrum position. J.D. Power's recent wireless customer satisfaction survey scores us at 785, a 12-point year-over-year gain, directly linked to this churn reduction.

Positive factors include our "Stay Connected Loyalty" program, pairing unlimited 5G data with perks like Disney+ Hotstar and Paramount+, which cut voluntary churn by 25% among millennials and Gen Z. Fixed Mobile Convergence adoption rose 18% quarter-over-quarter, with wireline broadband users switching to our mobile plans showing 40% lower churn rates. We navigated headwinds like inflation's 1.2% ARPU erosion in prepaid segments, where churn ticked up to 2.1%, through AI-driven predictive models analyzing over 500 behavioral signals. These efforts identified and retained 65,000 at-risk customers with tailored offers, preventing $45 million in annual revenue loss.

Broadband churn improved to 0.95%, down 8 basis points quarter-over-quarter and 14 basis points year-over-year—our strongest since pandemic-era cord-cutting. This segment, comprising 42% of revenue, stabilized following our $2.5 billion fiber-to-the-x investments. Rural penetration grew 22% through Open Access partnerships, similar to Altice USA's approach, keeping rural churn at 1.1% versus 0.85% in urban areas.

Upside came from DOCSIS 4.0 upgrades in 15 million homes, providing symmetrical gigabit speeds and reducing service complaints by 30%. Bundling with our ad-supported streaming tier retained 72% of potential switchers to standalone ISPs like EarthLink. Competitive pressures from Comcast's Xfinity Mobile caused a slight 0.2% uptick in multi-play disconnects, but wholesale dark fiber agreements with hyperscalers like AWS improved reliability and contained it.

Video and streaming churn held at 2.45%, flat sequentially but down 35 basis points year-over-year—trending down for four quarters amid streaming competition. Household pay-TV bundle churn fell to 1.8%, resilient against Netflix and Disney+.

Regionally, North America (65% of subscribers) saw U.S. postpaid mobile at 0.72%, aided by T-Mobile merger-like synergies from our 2023 mid-tier asset acquisition. Canada was at 0.85%, echoing Rogers-Shaw dynamics. EMEA (20%) faced 1.35% due to EU roaming rules and Vodafone/Three merger effects, but 5G Standalone in Germany and the UK cut it 20 basis points with low-latency gaming bundles. APAC/LATAM (15%) had prepaid at 3.2% from Jio/Claro pricing battles in India/Brazil, mitigated by eSIM auto-renewals reducing voluntary losses 15%.

To build on this, we're intensifying tech-led retention. Our GenAI churn prediction tool on Snowflake and Amdocs now hits 92% accuracy, up from 82%, delivering personalized "Churn Buster" incentives with 28% retention gains in tests. We're aiming for 70% FMC penetration by year-end, targeting blended churn below 1.0% in FY24. Capex efficiencies from 5G mmWave densification and Open RAN trials with Nokia/Samsung should boost NPS by 10 points. We're tracking Charter's fiber shift and AT&T's HBO Max plays, but our 1.3x industry-leading NPS sets us up for gains. For Q3, we guide blended churn to 1.05-1.10%, full-year at 1.15%—18 basis points ahead of consensus—supporting raised FY24 EBITDA of $18.2-18.5 billion, with every 10 basis points saving $120 million in free cash flow.

Shifting to our spectrum assets, the foundation of our wireless and media operations, we hold about 1,450 MHz of low-, mid-, and high-band spectrum nationwide, second only to Verizon, including 280 MHz premium C-band from the 2021 FCC auction for $9.6 billion across 80 Partial Economic Areas. Utilization averaged 78% this quarter, up from 68% last year, propelled by 5G rollouts and efficiency improvements.

By band: Low-band (600 MHz and 850 MHz) at 82% utilization, delivering 45 Mbps rural throughput via Dynamic Spectrum Sharing for 4G/5G layering—a 15% year-over-year rise. Midwest/Plains utilization nears 90% peaks, backing $1.2 billion Rural Digital Opportunity Fund wins for 5 million locations.

Mid-band (C-band 3.7-3.98 GHz, 2.5 GHz Sprint legacy) hits 85% in urban/suburban areas, with 650 Mbps median speeds from 100 MHz carriers plus PCS, topping T-Mobile per Ookla. Efficiency rose 25% to 4.2 bits/Hz via massive MIMO at 15,000+ sites. Northeast Corridor reaches 92%, driven by private 5G for logistics.

High-band mmWave (26/39 GHz) at 55%, focused on stadiums, arenas, and FWA in 350 markets, adding 450,000 broadband subs year-to-date at 20% higher ARPU. Sun Belt peaks at 75% for 2 Gbps+ AR/VR trials with Disney and NovaVR.

Capacity grew 35% year-over-year to 12.5 exabytes monthly, ahead of 8% subscriber growth via slicing for media—video at 65% payload with <10 ms latency. Rural lags at 62%, but n71 CBRS helps.

Future plans emphasize optimization, acquisition, and innovation. We'll refarm 160 MHz AWS-3 to 5G SA by year-end for 20% capacity boost, with Open RAN pilots yielding 30% OpEx savings for gaming like Xbox. Acquisitions get $4.5 billion from $18 billion capex, targeting 3.45-3.55 GHz DoD return (100 MHz), CBRS PALs, Dish secondary buys, and European 700 MHz via Vodafone JV. Innovation includes $800 million in 6G sub-THz for holographic media, enabling synchronized ads for $500 million revenue by 2026. This sustains 48% wireless EBITDA margins through 5G-to-6G.

On operating expense management, we achieved $425 million in year-over-year savings, expanding adjusted EBITDA margins 220 basis points to 38.5%. In this competitive telecom/media arena—with 5G auctions and streaming battles akin to AT&T-Time Warner or Netflix/Disney+—this discipline is essential.

Network operations drove 45% or $191 million: AI predictive maintenance via NetOptix cut outages 32% and dispatches 28%, saving $85 million. U.S. copper consolidation via dark fiber swaps saved $62 million; 5G small cells cut power 22%. EMEA tower co-locations saved $34 million; APAC divestitures $10 million.

Content/programming yielded $106 million (25%): Renegotiated Disney/Paramount fees saved $45 million; TeleStream+ bundling cut CAC 21% to $45/sub; sunset 15 channels saved $32 million; originals ROI 2.5x on $150 million. AI recommendations boosted retention 14%, saving $29 million; LATAM dubbing cut 25% or $12 million.

SG&A/back-office: $85 million (20%) via 4,200 role reductions (3.2% YoY, $52 million), RPA for billing ($22 million), digitized B2B (27% cut). U.S. CHIPS Act credits $8 million; Europe procurement $11 million.

Vendor consolidation: $43 million (10%), top suppliers to 32, improving DPO to 68 days ($120 million working capital).

These savings grew EBITDA 14% to $2.15 billion quarterly equivalent, FCF 22% to $1.1 billion, funding buybacks at 2.8x leverage. We're reallocating $300 million to FY24 capex for Open RAN (40% savings) and edge media.

For capital expenditure guidance on network investments, our FY24 total remains $17.5-18.5 billion, with 85% or $15-15.8 billion to networks—a 3% uptick from 2023's $14.6 billion amid easing inflation.

Wireless: 55% or $8.3-8.7 billion for 5G SA (85% top metros), C-band densification post $2.1 billion Auction 108, mmWave urban upgrades, Open RAN pilots (20% sites by Q4 2025), securing $450 million enterprise private 5G.

Fiber/fixed: $4.5-4.8 billion (28%) for 4 million more FTTH passings to 35 million; Southeast greenfield; Europe NG-PON2 $800 million.

Media/edge: $2.5-2.9 billion (17%) for CDN, edge DCs with Equinix/AWS for TeleStream+ (28 million subs), FWA ramp to 2.5 million 2025 adds.

North America 72% ($10.8-11.4 billion), ARPU $55.20 (+4.2%); EMEA 18%, APAC 10%. Capex/revenue 16-17%; 2025 flattens at $15.5 billion midpoint toward SDN/6G. RootMetrics 98.7% availability supports 10%+ EPS CAGR.

Finally, subscriber and revenue guidance: Q3 postpaid mobile net adds 450,000, FY24 1.8 million (+12%); 65 million 5G connections (+25%), ARPU $55.50 (+2.5%). Broadband FWA/fiber 350,000 Q3, 1.4 million FY (+18%); gigabit 40%. NexStream 2.2 million Q3 paid adds, FY 8.5 million (+22%); total video 28 million (+5%).

Q3 revenue $15.8 billion (+4.2%): wireless $9.1 billion (+3.8%), broadband $4.2 billion (+5.1%), media $2.5 billion (+6.7%). FY24 $62.5 billion (+4.5%): wireless $36.5 billion (+4%), broadband $16.8 billion (+5.5%), media $9.2 billion (+5.8%); margins +50 bps to 42%. Converged Edge, Open RAN, AI pricing fuel this; FCF $12 billion for 75% shareholder returns.

Dr. Lena Patel: Thank you. I would like to provide an update on our network performance. We have made significant progress in expanding our 5G coverage to 85% of key markets, with mid-band utilization at 85% enabling 650 Mbps speeds. Our network reliability metrics continue to improve, with unplanned outages down 32% from AI optimizations, and we are seeing increased data usage across our customer base—video traffic at 65% of payload. We are also actively working on enhancing our cybersecurity infrastructure alongside edge computing for low-latency media. Our team's dedication to spectral efficiency and Open RAN has been instrumental in achieving these results, supporting FWA growth and private networks.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from Simon Bates with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Simon Bates: Good morning. Can you discuss the competitive landscape and your strategy for maintaining low churn rates amid pricing pressures?

Alex Rivera: Certainly, Simon. The landscape remains intense with peers like T-Mobile and Comcast pushing aggressive bundles, but our multi-faceted approach—combining 5G Ultra Wideband superiority, FMC bundles reaching 70% penetration target, and AI churn prediction at 92% accuracy—has driven blended churn to 1.12%, well below industry 1.45%. Programs like Stay Connected Loyalty and GenAI incentives have retained key demographics, positioning us for share gains as we monitor Charter and AT&T moves.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Lisa Wong: Hi, thanks for taking my question. What are your expectations for subscriber growth in the next quarter, and how will that impact EBITDA margins?

Michael Chen: We anticipate strong momentum, Lisa, with Q3 postpaid mobile adds at 450,000 and broadband 350,000, aligning to FY24 totals of 1.8 million and 1.4 million respectively, plus 8.5 million NexStream paid subs. This drives Q3 revenue to $15.8 billion and FY $62.5 billion, with margins expanding 50 basis points to 42% from opex savings and ARPU growth to $55.50, bolstered by $425 million efficiencies and spectrum-driven capacity.

Operator: Our next question comes from Raj Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Raj Patel: Can you provide an update on your fiber deployment plans and the expected ROI on those investments?

Dr. Lena Patel: Absolutely, Raj. We're guiding $4.5-4.8 billion to fiber, adding 4 million passings to 35 million total, with 95% take rates in new Southeast builds. ROI accelerates via 40% gigabit adoption and FWA synergies, mirroring Verizon FiOS—expecting payback under 4 years as symmetrical speeds cut churn 30% and enable $450 million enterprise wins, with Open RAN enhancing efficiency.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Alex, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Alex Rivera: Thank you. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value. Thank you for your time and interest in NovaTel Communications.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
